extra.message: The user-controlled `term` query parameter is concatenated directly into a raw SQL string (`title ILIKE '%${term}%'`) passed to `db.execute(sql.raw(...))`. Any authenticated user can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. `' OR 1=1 UNION SELECT ...`) to read or modify arbitrary database rows, including password hashes.

`searchGradesAdvanced` builds SQL conditions with `sql.raw(\`${field} ${criterion.op} '${criterion.value}'\`)` where `field`, `op` and `value` come from the attacker-supplied `criteria` object. The resulting fragment is embedded into a raw query, allowing authenticated instructors/students to inject arbitrary SQL.

`getCohortRosterFiltered` reads the `cohortRosterView` cookie, JSON-parses it, and splices every `field`/`value` pair from the cookie into `sql.raw(...)` (`${field} = '${value}'`). The cookie is fully attacker-controlled, so an instructor/TA can inject arbitrary SQL to read or alter any table.

`previewWeightedRubricScoreAction` passes the instructor-supplied `weightingRule` form value directly to `new Function("scores", \`return ${weightingRule}\`)` and executes it server-side. This is arbitrary JavaScript code execution (RCE) by any user with the school_admin/instructor/teaching_assistant role.

The `preset` value from the request JSON body is interpolated into the command string `spawn(\`pandoc ${sourcePath} ${preset} -o ${outputPath}\`, { shell: true })`. Any authenticated user (no role check) can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; curl ... | sh`) to achieve OS command injection on the server.

`execSync(\`pandoc ${sourcePath} -o ${outputPath}\`)` is invoked with `outputFormat` (from the request body) embedded in `outputPath` without validation or shell-escaping. A student can inject shell commands via `outputFormat` (e.g. `pdf; cat /etc/passwd #`) to execute arbitrary OS commands.

The `filename` query parameter is joined with UPLOAD_DIR (`join(UPLOAD_DIR, filename)`) and read with `readFileSync`, with no basename/containment check and no ownership verification of the submission. Any authenticated user can pass `../../.env`, `/etc/passwd`, or an absolute path to read arbitrary files on the server.

`retrieveFromCategoryArchive` builds `join(UPLOAD_DIR, record.category, record.originalName)` and reads it. `category`/`originalName` are attacker-controlled at upload time (no sanitization in POST), and an absolute or `../`-containing `originalName` escapes the upload tree, giving any authenticated user arbitrary file read. The file owner is also never checked (IDOR).

`fetch(sourceUrl)` is called with a fully attacker-controlled URL and the response body + content-type are returned to the caller. Any authenticated user can make the server fetch internal/cloud-metadata addresses (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, http://localhost:*) and read the responses, i.e. full SSRF.

`submitGradeDisputeResolution` performs no authentication or authorization at all (no getSessionUser/requireRole). An unauthenticated attacker can change the `totalPoints` of any grade, set `isDraft=false`, and fabricate grade history for any `gradeId`.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Any authenticated user can POST arbitrary `criteria` (including `{}` → no WHERE clause) to fetch every enrollment in the school, and each row is returned with the full related `student` and `cohort` objects (`with: { student: true, cohort: true }`). Because the `users` relation includes `passwordHash`, this leaks all users' bcrypt password hashes and PII school-wide.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: `applyVendorProfileSync` trusts the client-supplied `x-vendor-role: district_admin` and `x-vendor-student-id` headers as its only 'authentication'; the vendored SDK stub `gradeSyncSdk.fetchSyncResult` always returns `{ access: true }`, and the merged `updates` body (arbitrary keys incl. `role`, `passwordHash`) is written to any user id. This allows an unauthenticated attacker to overwrite any account's role/password hash (full account takeover).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: `verifyResourceGrant` honors a token header claiming `alg: "none"` and returns the attacker-chosen payload without verifying any signature. `/api/cohorts/roster-grant/[token]` calls this verifier with no session/role gate, so an unauthenticated attacker can forge a token (`header.alg=none`, arbitrary `cohortId`, future `exp`) and read the full student roster of any cohort.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: `restoreProfileBackupAction` spreads an attacker-supplied JSON `backup` directly into the caller's users row (`db.update(users).set({ ...snapshot })`). A low-privileged student can set `role: "school_admin"`, `isActive`, `email`, or even a known `passwordHash` on their own account, achieving privilege escalation / account takeover. (A field-restricted variant `restoreProfileFieldsAction` exists, showing the intended allowlist.)

`updateSubmissionDraftAction` spreads every field of the client-supplied multipart form into `db.update(submissions).set({ ...fields })`. A student can set arbitrary submission columns (status, assignmentId, filePath, studentId, submittedAt, etc.) on their submission, e.g. move the submission to a different cohort's assignment or flip status to bypass grading locks.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: Notification `message` is rendered with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. The message body is written unsanitized by `broadcastCohortAnnouncement` (Handlebars output inserted as-is into the DB), so an instructor can store arbitrary HTML/`<script>` that executes in every recipient student's browser (stored XSS).

`continueTo` (a query parameter) is passed unvalidated into `new URL(continueTo, req.url)` and used as the redirect target. An attacker can supply `continueTo=https://evil.example` to turn this authenticated endpoint into an open redirect for phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The uploaded emblem is written to `join(EMBLEM_DIR, artwork.name)` using the client-supplied original filename with no sanitization, size limit, or content validation, into the public web root. A filename containing `../` or an absolute path escapes `public/course-emblems`, enabling arbitrary file writes and, because uploaded HTML/SVG is served same-origin from `/course-emblems/`, stored XSS.

`x-device-label` (a client-controlled header) is used directly in `join(STATE_DIR, \`${deviceLabel}.json\`)` with no basename sanitization (compare the sibling `state-backup` route that does use `basename`), allowing an authenticated user to write JSON files outside the state directory via path traversal.

`expandEntities` processes `<!ENTITY name SYSTEM "uri">` declarations from attacker-controlled XML (the `widgetState` cookie is decoded with `decodeWidgetState`) and reads the referenced file with `fs.readFileSync`, honouring `file://` and absolute paths. This is a local file-read primitive (XXE-style); combined with other endpoints it can also be used as an error oracle.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: `queryEmployeeDirectory` splices the raw `searchTerm` into an LDAP filter `(cn=*${searchTerm}*)` with no escaping. LDAP metacharacters (`*`, `(`, `)`, NUL) in the term alter the filter semantics, enabling LDAP filter injection to enumerate directory entries. (The adjacent `findDirectoryMemberByEmail` correctly uses `escapeDirectoryFilterValue`.)

`pinDiscussionForPartnerEmbed` lets any authenticated user (no role or cohort-membership check) pin/unpin any discussion in the school by supplying an arbitrary `discussionId` (in contrast to `/api/discussions/moderate`, which checks cohortInstructors membership).

`viewSubmissionWorkDetail` returns any submission (text content, file name/path, status) for an attacker-supplied `submissionId` without verifying that the caller is the submission owner or an instructor of the cohort. Any authenticated student can read other students' submissions across cohorts (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: `renderDiscussionEmbedWidget` returns the full discussion record for an arbitrary `discussionId` with no enrollment/cohort-membership check, letting any authenticated user read discussion content from cohorts they do not belong to.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: `exportDiscussionThread` exports the title + content of any discussion given a discussionId, with no check that the caller is a member/instructor of the discussion's cohort — a cross-cohort information disclosure for any authenticated user.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: `getCohortRoster` requires only an instructor/TA role, not membership in the requested cohort (compare `/api/cohorts/waitlist`, which does check cohortInstructors). Any instructor/TA can pull the roster of every cohort, and because `with: { student: true }` returns full user rows, the response includes students' password hashes.

The grades/submissions export endpoints accept any `instructor` role but never scope the query to cohorts the caller teaches — an instructor (or TA) can export the entire school's grades and submission text content, a school-wide data exposure.

`verifyCohortInvite` has no authentication and no invite-code check: an unauthenticated caller who knows an email + cohortId can activate any pending enrollment (`UPDATE enrollments SET status='active'`), i.e. enroll arbitrary people into paid/limited cohorts.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: `redeemCohortInvite` similarly performs no authentication and ignores the invite code generated by `/api/cohorts/invite`: an unauthenticated attacker who supplies an email + cohortId activates that enrollment. Invite 'codes' are 6-digit and never stored or verified, so they provide no protection.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: `redeemOnboardingCode` rebinds the *existing* `session_token` cookie value to the target account (`UPDATE sessions SET userId = user.id WHERE token = existingToken`). If an attacker can plant a session cookie in a victim's browser, the victim's later code redemption upgrades the attacker's known token to the victim's session — classic session fixation.

API keys are generated with `Math.random().toString(36)...`, which is not cryptographically secure. The resulting key is the sole bearer credential for the grade-sync integration (see verifyGradeSyncKey), so it should be generated with `crypto.randomBytes`.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: `issueTemporaryStaffCredential` stores the password as a plain MD5 of an 8-hex-char (≈32-bit) onboarding code and also never sends the code to the user. Such a short code hashed with unsalted single-pass MD5 is trivially brute-forced offline, and the credential flow leaks plaintext temp passwords into audit/log paths.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: When `ROSTER_GRANT_SECRET` is unset, token signatures fall back to the hardcoded value `roster-grant-dev-secret`. Combined with the `alg: none` acceptance in `verifyResourceGrant`, deployed instances without the env var have forgeable roster-grant tokens. Similar hardcoded fallback secrets exist in `requestIntegrity.ts:3` and `draftCipher.ts:6`.
